summary: Vicente Fatone worked in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Calcutta (1937–1938). He held professorships at the National University of the Litoral (1929) and the National University of La Plata (1940), later joining the University of Buenos Aires (1960).

Victor A. van Bijlert is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Leiden University (1975–1987). He held posts at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies, IIM Calcutta, Leiden University, and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (until 2021).

Historian Victor B. Lieberman studied at Yale University (BA ~1963–1967) and SOAS University of London (PhD ~1970–1976). In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History and Professor of Asian and Comparative History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago. He founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education in 2005 and served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia.
French philosopher Victor Cousin studied at Lycée Charlemagne (until 1810) and Pensionnat normal (~1810–1812). He held an academic post at the University of Paris from around 1815 to 1851.

Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Temple University in 2004. He served as Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College (attested 2007).

Victor Goloubew worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at Saint Petersburg University and earning his PhD from Heidelberg University (1901–1904). He taught at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1920–1943).

Victor H. Mair studied at Dartmouth, the University of Washington, SOAS, and Harvard under Patrick Hanan and James Robert Hightower. A scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, he taught at Harvard and was appointed at the University of Pennsylvania in 1979.

Victor Hehn worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1830–1834), briefly held a post there around 1851, and later worked at the National Library of Russia from 1855 to 1873.

Victor Henry was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Strasbourg, Burgundy, and Paris under Abel Bergaigne. He held appointments at the universities of Lille, Douai, and Paris, becoming Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Grammar at the Sorbonne in 1894.

Victor Herbert Jackson was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He joined the Indian Education Service in 1900, taught at Presidency University (~1900–1907), and served as Principal of Patna College (~1917–1927).

Linguist Victor Michels studied in Berlin under Paul Deussen, in Heidelberg under Hermann Osthoff, and earned his PhD in Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and Ernst Windisch. He later held posts at Göttingen (1892) and Jena (1895).

Victor Turner studied at University College London (BA 1946–1949) and the University of Manchester (PhD ~1950–1955). Active in religious studies and anthropology, he held posts at the Rhodes-Livingstone Institute, Manchester, Cornell, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia.

Victoria Vertogradova is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson. She served as Chief Research Fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts as a pandit and supervisor of collation at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1941–1943).

Vidya Dehejia studied at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and Cambridge (PhD 1968). A scholar of Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, she held posts at Sydney, Hong Kong, the Smithsonian Institution, and Columbia University, where she was appointed professor in 2002.

Vidya Niwas Mishra studied at Allahabad under K. C. Chattopadhyaya, Gorakhpur, and under Paul Thieme. An Indologist and linguist, he was Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, visiting professor in California and Washington, and Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.
Vijay Singh is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from Panjab University (1998–2002). He served at Panjab University beginning in 1994 as Professor and Chairperson.
Vijaya Indra Suri was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who succeeded Vijaya Dharma Suri (attested 1933). He founded the Prakrit Text Society and taught Charlotte Krause.
Vijayalakshmi Mani is an Indology and archaeology scholar who conducted PhD research at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.
